title: Calibration-guided inference policy manager for mixed-precision paths
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a runtime policy manager that integrates per-model calibration signals and lightweight on-request probes to choose a safe, cost-effective execution path across FP16/FP8/INT8 kernels. The policy manager will: 1) fetch the model's calibrated quant profile (scale ranges, per-layer sensitivity) at request time, 2) run a cheap calibration probe for ambiguous inputs (first N tokens or a hashing-based fingerprint sample) to estimate drift/confidence, 3) compute a runtime path score that balances latency, cost, and an accuracy risk metric, and 4) select the kernel path or trigger a graceful fallback (higher-precision or shadow-validation) if the risk exceeds a model-configured threshold. This ticket covers the policy logic, runtime hooks, feature flags, and integration points with the kernel broker, KV cache, and telemetry ingestion pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime policy decides between FP16/FP8/INT8 on >99% of requests within 200us decision latency. 2) When policy triggers a fallback, end-to-end response latency remains within SLA degradation budget (defined in runtime-mixed-precision SLO doc). 3) No regression in measured quality on our calibration testset (statistical equivalence at 95% CI) after enabling the policy for a model. 4) Full observability: per-request path decision, confidence score, and fallback reason are surfaced to Console and available in traces. 5) Feature flag controls exist for per-model policy aggressiveness and probe budget.
implementation_notes:
- New component: policy-manager service (co-located in inference runtime process) exposing a compact API for decision input (model_id, quant_profile_hash, token_fingerprint, runtime_stats).
- Use existing quant-profile store (persisted configs from calibration pipeline) and cache TTL of 10m.
- Probe design: deterministic lightweight fingerprinting + up to 8-token micro-probe executed on a shadow thread with early-exit heuristics.
- Score composition: weighted sum of calibration-sensitivity, probe-confidence, recent telemetry error-rate, and latency-cost weight pulled from model config. Weights configurable via Console.
- Add adapters to kernel-broker to accept a "preferred_path" hint plus safety-disable flag to force fallback.
- Telemetry events: policy.decision, policy.probe.sample, policy.fallback.trigger, policy.path_latency.
- Implementation to include unit tests for scoring math, e2e harness against calibration dataset, and perf microbenchmarks for decision latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default. 2) Shadow mode (policy runs and logs decisions but does not affect execution) for 2 weeks across 5% of traffic for a target model family. 3) Gradual enable: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 3 days each, with automated rollback on accuracy regression or error-rate spike. 4) Canary of fallback policy (aggressive thresholds) limited to internal test accounts. 5) Post-rollout 2-week monitoring window and calibration re-run if drift observed.
telemetry: Events emitted as structured logs and traces. Required fields: request_id, model_id, quant_profile_version, probe_present (true/false), decision_path, decision_score, fallback_reason (if any), decision_latency_ms. Dashboards: per-model decision distribution, fallback rate, probe hit-rate, correlated quality regressions on calibration testset. Alerts: fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 1h or decision_latency P95 > 500ms.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for policy scoring and boundary cases.
- Integration tests: policy + kernel-broker + KV cache in CI with synthetic workloads (low/high sensitivity layers).
- Regression tests: run preexisting calibration test-suite and new adversarial input set; require no significant drop.
- Perf tests: microbench for decision latency at 50k QPS equivalent using stress harness.
- Shadow run validation: compare policy decisions against ground-truth high-precision baseline and produce per-layer blame reports.
